## System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Canonical["Canonical Unikernel Image"]
        Core[Common Execution Core]
        AL[Adaptation Layer]
        API[API Reshaping Engine]
        Proto[Protocol Translator]
        Cfg[Config Model Mapper]
        RT[Runtime Behavior Adapter]
    end

    subgraph Profiles["Adaptation Profiles"]
        P1[Tenant A Profile]
        P2[Tenant B Profile]
        P3[Platform C Profile]
    end

    subgraph Personalities["Exposed Personalities"]
        E1[REST + K8s Personality]
        E2[gRPC + OpenStack Personality]
        E3[MQTT + Edge Personality]
    end

    P1 --> AL
    P2 --> AL
    P3 --> AL

    AL --> API
    AL --> Proto
    AL --> Cfg
    AL --> RT

    API --> Core
    Proto --> Core
    Cfg --> Core
    RT --> Core

    Core --> E1
    Core --> E2
    Core --> E3
```

## Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as Client Environment
    participant Profile as Adaptation Profile
    participant Layer as Adaptation Layer
    participant Core as Execution Core
    participant Surface as External Personality

    Client->>Profile: Define interfaces and protocols
    Client->>Profile: Define resource model
    Client->>Profile: Define operational conventions
    Profile->>Layer: Submit profile at init
    Layer->>Layer: Parse expected APIs
    Layer->>Layer: Map communication protocols
    Layer->>Layer: Reshape config model
    Layer->>Core: Bind adapted interfaces
    Core->>Surface: Expose client-specific personality
    Client->>Surface: Interact via expected API
    Surface->>Core: Translate to canonical ops
    Core->>Surface: Return canonical result
    Surface->>Client: Deliver in client format
```

## Component Detail

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Build["Single Build Pipeline"]
        Src[Unified Codebase] --> Img[Canonical Image]
    end

    subgraph Deploy["Deployment Targets"]
        Img --> D1[Cloud Tenant A]
        Img --> D2[Cloud Tenant B]
        Img --> D3[Edge Platform C]
    end

    subgraph Adapt["Per-Target Adaptation"]
        D1 --- A1[Profile A: REST, K8s, x86]
        D2 --- A2[Profile B: gRPC, OpenStack, ARM]
        D3 --- A3[Profile C: MQTT, Bare Metal, RISC-V]
    end
```

## Adaptation Layer Internals

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph ProfileParsing["Profile Parsing"]
        PP[Profile Ingestion]
        IV[Interface Validator]
    end

    subgraph Reshaping["Dynamic Reshaping"]
        AE[API Endpoint Generator]
        PT[Protocol Binding]
        CM[Config Schema Transform]
        RB[Runtime Behavior Selection]
    end

    subgraph Security["Security Posture"]
        SP[Unified Security Policy]
        Audit[Audit Logging]
    end

    PP --> IV
    IV --> AE
    IV --> PT
    IV --> CM
    IV --> RB

    AE --> SP
    PT --> SP
    CM --> SP
    RB --> SP
    SP --> Audit
```

## State Diagram

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Dormant: Image deployed
    Dormant --> ProfileLoading: Profile received
    ProfileLoading --> Validating: Parse profile
    Validating --> Adapting: Validation passed
    Validating --> Rejected: Invalid profile
    Rejected --> Dormant: Await new profile
    Adapting --> APIBinding: Reshape APIs
    APIBinding --> ProtocolBinding: Map protocols
    ProtocolBinding --> ConfigMapping: Transform config
    ConfigMapping --> Ready: Adaptation complete
    Ready --> Serving: Accept client requests
    Serving --> Serving: Handle requests
    Serving --> Adapting: Profile updated
    Serving --> [*]: Shutdown
```

TASK: Create mermaid.js diagrams for this invention. INSTRUCTION: Output ONLY mermaid code blocks. No explanations. MERMAID RULES (for PNG / mermaid-cli compatibility): - Do NOT use HTML line breaks in the diagram: no
,
, or similar anywhere in the mermaid source (including inside node labels). They break many renderers and image export. - Use shorter labels, multiple nodes, or subgraphs instead of forcing line breaks inside one label. INVENTION: --- invention-id: invention-20260623-163539 company: RedHat created: 2026-06-23T16:35:45 --- # Invention Idea We propose a polymorphic unikernel architecture in which a single canonical unikernel image serves multiple tenants, platforms, or deployment environments. Rather than distributing architecture-specific or customer-specific variants, clients provide an adaptation profile describing their expected interfaces, protocols, resource models, and operational conventions. Upon initialization, an adaptation layer dynamically reshapes exposed APIs, communication mechanisms, configuration models, and runtime behaviors to match the client's environment while preserving a common internal execution core. The unikernel therefore presents different external personalities to different consumers while maintaining a single maintainable codebase and security posture. This enables large-scale deployment of a unified unikernel that automatically conforms to customer-specific requirements without requiring separate builds or bespoke implementations. OUTPUT: ## System Architecture `mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Input[Data Sources] A[Source A] B[Source B] end subgraph Process[Processing] C[Tracker] D[Detector] end subgraph Output[Results] E[Clean Data] F[Alerts] end A --> C B --> C C --> D D --> E D --> F ` ## Sequence Diagram `mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Source participant T as Tracker participant D as Detector participant Sys as System S->>T: Submit Data T->>D: Validate D->>Sys: Forward or Block ` Create diagrams specific to THIS invention.
